items.title: Ni Hsin shifts into high gear with EV diversification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ni Hsin Group Bhd is diversifying its business into electric vehicles (EVs) as it seeks to scale up its electric motorcycle operations, OEM assembly and market reach. Ni Hsin, in a Bursa Malaysia filing today, said the proposed diversification will cover EV assembly, promotion and marketing of EVs. The company wants to build on a business it has operated since 2021 through its subsidiaries Ni Hsin EV Tech Sdn Bhd and EVSend Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Nursery worker to be charged over alleged mistreatment of toddler in Temerloh
items.summary: TEMERLOH: The childcare centre worker detained over the alleged rough treatment of a 2-year-old girl at a nursery in Mentakab here last week will be charged tomorrow. Temerloh police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the woman would be charged under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001. The suspect was arrested on Sept 5, several hours after the victim's mother lodged a police report alleging that her daughter had been subjected to rough treatment by a caregiver at the nursery.

items.title: Sarawak heli crash: A look at the Flying Doctor Service
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: For many isolated communities in Malaysia's interior, the Health Ministry's Flying Doctor Service (FDS) is often the difference between receiving healthcare and none at all. Apart from the pilot, those onboard comprised four Health Ministry personnel, namely one medical officer, an assistant medical officer and two nurses. According to the FDS guidelines for Sabah and Sarawak, each mobile aeromedical team consists of a four-person medical crew, comprising one medical officer, one assistant medical officer, and two community nurses.

items.title: Asia is poised to take up 70pct of Canadian oil exports, pipeline executive says
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Asia, led by China, is expected to buy 70 per cent of Canadian crude oil exports after the country's only pipeline that provides access to the continent expands its capacity by a third by the end of 2028, a Canadian industry executive said on Tuesday. * Canada's oil output, the world's fourth-largest, this year is set to exceed last year's record of 5.3 million barrels per day, according to Canada's energy regulator. * Mark Maki, chief executive officer of the pipeline operator Trans Mountain, said the pipeline expansion would add 90,000 barrels per day of transport capacity in the fourth quarter, and another 210,000 barrels per day by the end of 2028.

items.title: Moody's sees ongoing surge in Africa's private credit market
items.summary: LONDON: Africa's private credit market is set for further expansion as companies and infrastructure projects seek alternatives to constrained bank lending, credit ratings firm Moody's said in a report on Tuesday. The continent's private credit industry remains small but has grown rapidly in recent years, with assets under management rising to US$5.6 billion at the end of 2025 from US$1.8 billion in 2020, according to the report. Moody's said demand would continue to be supported by the region's persistent financing gap, underdeveloped capital markets and limits on banks' ability and willingness to provide long-term financing, particularly for infrastructure projects, medium-sized companies and small businesses.

items.title: Malaysia’s SMART team arrives in Nepal disaster zone, begins drone reconnaissance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) arrived in Dhunche, Nepal, today to establish a forward base and begin aerial reconnaissance operations using drones in the disaster-stricken area. According to a statement issued by the Home-Based Support Team (HBST) of MAS01 SMART, under the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), the 10-member team, led by Inspector Abdullah Ahmad Sobri, travelled to the location aboard an MI-17 helicopter. “Dhunche serves as the tactical forward base for managing disaster operations in the Rasuwa area, covering Timure, Syafrubesi, Dhunche and Mailung.

items.title: Gold subdued as oil rises, investors await key US inflation data
items.summary: Spot gold fell 0.1 per cent to US$4,400.66 per ounce by 1148 GMT, after rising as much as US$4,442.70 earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.7 per cent to US$4,445.20. "Gold trades cautiously today, caught between Fed rate hike bets and dollar softness.

items.title: Elderly man killed after being hit by SUV in Assam Jawa
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR: An elderly man was killed after he was thrown from his motorcycle when it was hit by a sports utility vehicle (SUV) at KM42.7 of the Klang-Teluk Intan Road near Assam Jawa here today. Kuala Selangor deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Ambia Nordin said the 3.50pm accident resulted in the 67-year-old victim dying at the scene. He said the crash involved a Perodua Kembara SUV and a Yamaha Ego LC motorcycle.

items.title: Public Bank offers RM1.29 a share to take Hong Kong listed unit private
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Public Bank Bhd is proposing to privatise its 73.23 per cent-owned Hong Kong-listed subsidiary Public Financial Holdings Ltd at HK$2.50 (RM1.29) a share via a scheme of arrangement. Public Bank said the offer price will not be increased. Public Financial's businesses span banking and financial services, stockbroking, investment property leasing, financing for taxi and public light-bus purchasers and taxi trading and leasing.

items.title: Husband told of Dr Ainul's death in Sarawak heli crash
items.summary: KOTA BARU: "Our family was contacted by the Health Ministry (MOH) this afternoon and informed that Dr Ainul had died." Nureez Mohd Pauzi, Dr Ainul's sister-in-law, said Dr Ainul had been identified as one of the passengers on the helicopter reported to have crashed and caught fire near Long Lellang Airport in Ulu Baram here this afternoon. She said the call from the MOH was made to Dr Ainul's husband, Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik, at around 4pm.

items.title: 'Dr Ainul' confirmed as among deceased in Sarawak heli crash
items.summary: Medical Officer Dr Ainul Baroah Kamaruddin, from Kelantan, was among those onboard the aircraft. She was among five people, including the pilot, on the flight. A picture of Dr Ainul, seated in a helicopter with others believed to be Health Ministry personnel, was widely circulated today following the crash.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Status of five aboard Flying Doctor Service helicopter still unknown after Sarawak crash
items.summary: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the helicopter, which departed from Miri, was carrying a pilot and four MOH health personnel — a medical officer, medical assistant and two nurses — who were on official duty. “Based on the initial information received, the flight that departed from Miri was operated by one pilot and carried four MOH health personnel, namely one medical officer, one medical assistant and two nurses who were on official duty,” he said in a statement. CAAM said the BO-105 helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service flight with five people on board, including the pilot.

items.title: Locally assembled EX90: Volvo's electric flagship arrives
items.summary: VOLVO Car Malaysia has launched the evolved EX90, Volvo's fully electric seven-seat flagship SUV, with the locally assembled model positioned as a new benchmark for premium electric mobility. Volvo's flagship continues the brand's safety-first philosophy through its Safe Space Technology, combining radars, sensors and ultrasonic sensors to create a detailed real-time view around the vehicle. The EX90 also features the latest Pilot Assist and Park Pilot Assist, adding enhanced driver support and collision-avoidance capabilities.

items.title: Trump sparks fury with post of map with Canada, Iceland as part of US
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump has sparked fury by posting a map that seemingly showed Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico and the Caribbean as part of the United States. The map showed the US, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico and the Caribbean coloured in with the US flag. Trump has also made insistent claims that Canada should become the 51st US state.

items.title: College student killed in Marang lorry crash
items.summary: The victim, Muhammad Afiq Izzuddin Azhar, 18, was pronounced dead at the scene following the accident at 1.10pm. Marang district police chief Superintendent Saari Mohamed said the accident involved an Isuzu lorry driven by a 34-year-old man and a Honda C100 motorcycle ridden by the victim. The lorry, which was travelling behind the motorcycle, then struck the victim's motorcycle, he said.

items.title: Flying doctor helicopter was carrying four Health Ministry personnel, pilot - Dzulkefly
items.summary: MIRI: The Health Ministry Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter that crashed here today was carrying four ministry personnel and a pilot. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said those on board were a medical officer, assistant medical officer and two nurses, who were on official duty. "Search and rescue (SAR) teams, together with medical personnel and the Fire and Rescue Department, are at the scene and the operation is ongoing," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Netanyahu under fire over report UAE warned of Oct 7 attack
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israeli opposition leaders on Tuesday called Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu unfit to serve after a report that the United Arab Emirates had warned him before the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack. "Netanyahu received dozens of warnings for Oct 7 and ignored them all. He is unfit," Eisenkot wrote on X. Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister also running in elections, said Netanyahu "bears personal and direct responsibility" for the deaths on Oct 7, the deadliest attack in Israeli history.

items.title: Budget 2027 should prioritise high-quality jobs to boost disposable income
items.summary: Prof Dr Mohd Abdullah Jusoh, of the Department of Logistics Management and Business Administration, Faculty of Defence Studies and Management, Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM), said economic stimulus measures should shift towards empowering the workforce with skills that would enable them to become self-reliant and earn higher incomes. He said financial assistance schemes such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) are effective in easing the people's financial burden and providing an immediate economic boost, but a long-term strategy requires the development of new economic engines. Commenting on the national economic outlook, Mohd Abdullah said Malaysia's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of six per cent in the second quarter of 2026 reflected an encouraging performance compared with World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates of between 2.5 and three per cent.

items.title: Green factors increasingly shape Malaysians' property decisions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sustainability and climate resilience are increasingly influencing Malaysians' property decisions, alongside price, size and location, according to PropertyGuru Malaysia's first half of 2026 consumer sentiment study. The study found that 86 per cent of Malaysians consider sustainable features important when buying or renting a home. Family and life-stage needs are also influencing property decisions, with 64 per cent of Malaysians living with a spouse, 38 per cent with parents, 38 per cent with young children and 21 per cent with adult children.

items.title: Turkish Airlines will be new Liverpool shirt sponsor in £300m deal
items.summary: LONDON, Sept 8 — Turkish Airlines will become Liverpool’s new front-of-shirt sponsor from the start of the 2027/28 season, the Premier League giants announced today. In February, Liverpool announced record revenues of more than £700 million for the most recent financial year, and were the highest-placed Premier League club in the Deloitte Football Money League. Liverpool were the first major English professional football club to have a shirt sponsor, when Japanese electronics company Hitachi had its name displayed across the club’s strip back in 1979.

items.title: Huawei heads to trial in US over its business dealings in Iran
items.summary: NEW YORK: Eight years after US prosecutors secretly charged China's Huawei Technologies with defrauding HSBC and other banks over its business with Iran, the case is finally heading for trial. Huawei also faces charges for conspiring to steal trade secrets from five US technology companies, and is accused of lying about its dealings in North Korea and supplying surveillance equipment to Iran to track protesters during 2009 anti-government demonstrations in Tehran. Convictions on the Iran-related charges would bolster Washington's case for having placed Huawei, one of China's leading technology companies, on a US trade blacklist in 2019, citing alleged criminal conduct that threatened national security.

items.title: Penang police chief: No compromise on misconduct
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said integrity, discipline and honesty were essential to policing duties. Speaking at the September monthly assembly at the Penang police contingent headquarters here today, Lim said there would be no compromise on abuse of power, extortion or attempts to shield criminals. Also present were Penang deputy police chief Datuk Abdul Rahman Kassim, state Criminal Investigation Department chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Zailanni Amit, Special Branch chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Zakaria A. Rahim, Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Helmi Aris, department and formation heads, district police chiefs, senior and junior police officers and civilian personnel.

items.title: East Coast poised to become food security hub, green economy leader – MIDA
items.summary: KUANTAN: Malaysia's East Coast region has strong potential to become a key hub for national food security and a leading centre for the green economy through greater investment in renewable energy. Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chief executive officer, Datuk Sikh Shamsul Ibrahim Sikh Abdul Majid, said smart farming, food processing, cold-chain infrastructure, and logistics could boost productivity and strengthen the country's food supply chain. He said the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) would further improve connectivity and market access for agrofood products by facilitating the movement of raw materials and finished products to wider markets.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez to be charged tomorrow over RCI-linked probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009. On Aug 27, the former TH chairman and former Treasury secretary-general were each remanded for seven days, until Sept 2, to assist investigations following disclosures related to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution. The RCI report, which examined TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, also identified investments requiring a forensic audit.

items.title: 81-year-old woman dies after being run over in Penang
items.summary: Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received information about the fatal accident at 3.50pm. "A vehicle, believed to be a car, then drove straight ahead and struck the victim before fleeing the scene without stopping," he said. Abdul Rozak said the woman was pronounced dead at the scene at 2.48pm after sustaining head injuries.

items.title: Flying Doctor Service helicopter carrying five crashes near Long Lellang airport
items.summary: KUCHING, 8 Sept — A BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) airport, about 929 kilometres north of Kuching, today. The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58 pm. The helicopter was operating a Flying Doctor Service flight with five people on board, including the pilot, CAAM said in a statement.

items.title: [UPDATED] Explainer: How remote is Long Lellang, where helicopter crashed?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Long Lellang, a remote settlement comprising two villages, Long Lellang A and Long Lellang B, came into the spotlight today after a helicopter crashed there. WHERE IS LONG LELLANG? HOW DO SUPPLIES REACH LONG LELLANG?

items.title: DAP wants equal constituency funding, starting with Penang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP wants the Penang government to enact a Constituency Development Fund (CDF) law to ensure development allocations are distributed fairly and equally to all assemblymen, regardless of political affiliation. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke, in a statement yesterday, said the party's Central Executive Committee (CEC) had resolved to ask the Penang government to enact a CDF Enactment, reflecting a reform agenda long championed by Pakatan Harapan (PH). Loke said the decision was among several reform matters discussed at the CEC's first meeting following the DAP National Conference on Aug 16.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng criticises Pas over lottery draw claims
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: DAP advisor Lim Guan Eng has criticised Pas over its claims concerning the party's stance on lottery draws. Lim said he was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 to eight times a year during the Pakatan Harapan administration from 2018 to 2020. "Pas is not honest and sincere when it fails to state that I was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 times to eight times a year when the PH government ruled from 2018 to 2020," he said in his Facebook posting.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 8, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed higher today, shrugging off renewed concerns over US monetary policy as gains spread across telecommunications, consumer, energy and banking stocks. The market remained resilient despite higher US Treasury yields, with broad-based gains driven by sectors supported by steady earnings and domestic demand. In the crypto market, Bitcoin fell to RM318,503.

items.title: Ringgit ends lower as oil prices rise, Fed decision looms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed lower against the US dollar on Tuesday, weighed by higher crude oil prices and cautious sentiment ahead of the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) next policy decision, an analyst said. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said elevated crude oil prices could strengthen the case for a Fed rate hike next week. "Other Asian currencies were also mixed, with the (US) dollar-yen hovering at 153 yen as expectations of a Bank of Japan rate hike next week gathered further momentum.

items.title: Porsche heritage meets the future at Luftwasser 2026
items.summary: PORSCHE Malaysia, represented by Sime Darby Auto Performance, joined hundreds of owners and enthusiasts at Luftwasser 2026: Icona Heritage, celebrating the marque's heritage, motorsport and future-facing technology. Porsche Malaysia highlighted this heritage through a display of racing cars from different eras, alongside current road models, illustrating how lessons from competition continue to influence Porsche's sports cars. The display also traced Porsche Malaysia's customer racing journey, featuring 911 GT3 Cup cars from the 997, 991 and current 992.2 generations.

items.title: Oil hits multi-week highs after Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities
items.summary: Brent crude futures were up US$1.39, or 1.43 per cent, at US$98.39 a barrel at 0956 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$93.73 a barrel, up US$2.25, or 2.46 per cent. Brent earlier rose to US$99.46, its highest since July 24, while WTI reached US$94.73, its highest since June 8.

items.title: Sarawak's Serian records very unhealthy API reading of 239
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today. Another 19 monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, with Sarawak accounting for five of the readings. Meanwhile, 31 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality, while three stations recorded good air quality.

items.title: Prasarana Integreated appoints Theta Edge's unit as network operator, strategic partner for Shah Alam line
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Theta Telecoms Sdn Bhd (TTEL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Theta Edge Bhd, has been appointed as the network operator and strategic partner for the development of a telecommunications common network infrastructure along the Shah Alam Line right of way. In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Theta Edge said TTEL accepted a letter of acceptance for the project on Sept 7, 2026, from Prasarana Integrated Development Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Prasarana Malaysia Bhd. The company said TTEL will also generate income by providing network telecommunication services by leveraging the Shah Alam line right of way granted.

items.title: MACC: Political Financing Bill should set clear penalties, ensure independent enforcement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Political Financing Bill should set clear penalties for political parties that breach contribution limits or fail to report their funding, while also establishing an independent regulatory body to ensure the law is effectively enforced. Deputy director of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) National Governance Planning Division Mohd Gunawan Che Ab Aziz said the matter is among five key governance principles to consider when drafting the Bill. He said the five principles comprised transparency, accountability, equity and fairness, independence, and inclusiveness and participation.

items.title: Zaid urges Putrajaya to safeguard Petronas interests in Sarawak talks
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 8 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to ensure the federal government and Petronas’ interests are protected as Putrajaya continues negotiations with Sarawak over the state’s oil and gas rights. In a post on X, Zaid expressed concern that political considerations could influence the government’s handling of Sarawak’s demands, particularly over Petros’ role as the state’s sole gas aggregator. “Anwar must not exchange political support for oil and gas to Sarawak,” he said.

items.title: Johor orders hunt for five feral dogs after girl mauled in Batu Pahat
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 8 — The Johor government has directed a large-scale operation to hunt and capture five feral dogs that attacked a two-year-old girl in Kampung Tambak in Batu Pahat last weekend. Johor religious committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khaled said efforts are being carried out by the Batu Pahat district office in collaboration with the Veterinary Services Department (DVS) and police. Mohd Fared said the immediate capture of the feral animals involved needs to be carried out to ensure that they are free of rabies.

items.title: Johari: Parliamentary Service Act gives Parliament greater scope to strengthen oversight of government
items.summary: CAMERON HIGHLANDS, Sept 8 — The implementation of the Parliamentary Service Act (PSA) provides Parliament with the scope to streamline its legislative role, including strengthening special select committees to assist the government in identifying shortcomings and addressing public issues, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul. He said the enactment of the PSA created a new environment after Parliament operated under executive oversight for 33 years, enabling the legislative body to play a more independent role in contributing to national prosperity. He said under the 10 ministry-related committees established, each is comprised of 12 Members of Parliament (MPs) representing both government and opposition backbenchers who do not hold ministerial or deputy ministerial posts.

items.title: Brothers get High Court leave to challenge DBKL approval for 39-storey towers near their Old Klang Road home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Two brothers have obtained High Court permission to challenge Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s approval for two 39-storey residential towers planned less than 11 metres from their home along Jalan Klang Lama. The judge also granted an interim stay on the development until the brothers’ application for a permanent stay is heard on October 8, despite an objection from the Attorney General’s Chambers. The proposed project is expected to have 1,544 residential units, with the brothers also seeking general damages and costs.

items.title: AI-powered traffic centre launched to boost safety, speed up response on three Klang Valley highways
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — With rising traffic volumes and frequent incidents putting greater pressure on highway operators, a new smart traffic control centre covering three major Klang Valley highways was launched today to enhance road safety and enable faster responses through real-time monitoring. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said past data showed that 85.4 per cent of traffic accidents on tolled expressways last year were attributed to human factors, while the remainder involved vehicle and environmental factors. Meanwhile, IJM’s AI-powered smart expressway traffic control centre integrates 144 CCTV cameras, 87 Video Incident Detection System units, 35 Automatic Number Plate Recognition units and 22 VMS units for the three aforementioned expressways.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Anak Krakatau ash could reach Malaysia, but risk remains low
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The risk of volcanic ash from Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau reaching Malaysia is currently low, although changes in wind direction and speed as well as possible further eruptions could affect its movement, MetMalaysia said today. “Information from global Volcanic Ash Advisory Centres (VAACs) also allows any potential movement of the ash into Malaysian airspace to be identified and communicated to the public promptly,” he said. Earlier, media reports said continued eruptions from Anak Krakatau since Friday had spread volcanic ash and prompted six airports to suspend flight operations.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Malaysia could see temperatures hit 40°C from January to May 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysia could experience extreme heat and dry weather from January to May next year, with temperatures in some areas potentially reaching 40°C as a very strong El Nino, or Super El Nino, is expected to develop towards the end of this year. He said past meteorological records showed that very strong El Nino episodes were often associated with higher temperatures, dry weather and a serious risk of haze, similar to conditions currently affecting the country. Mohd Hisham said there was about a 70 per cent probability that the intensity of the current El Nino would exceed the strength of any El Nino episode recorded since 1950.

items.title: Senior medical officer in Melaka remanded over RM1.5m knee implant supply probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — A senior medical officer has been remanded for five days to assist a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into alleged abuse of position involving the supply of knee implants worth about RM1.5 million. The remand order for the man, in his 50s, was issued by Ayer Keroh Magistrate Sharda Shienha Mohd Suleiman at the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court in Melaka this morning, Harian Metro reported. The public servant has been remanded until September 12 after MACC applied for the order to facilitate further investigations.

items.title: Anwar to chair MA63 meeting on Sabah’s 40pc revenue claim, says Hajiji
items.summary: Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said Sabah would host the meeting, which would also discuss outstanding claims and issues under MA63, Sinar Harian reported. He said this after a working visit to the Kunak Lipids Sdn Bhd Phytonutrient Extraction Plant in Kunak today. However, there are still other matters, including the 40 per cent payment,” he said.

items.title: Former minister released on MACC bail over Tabung Haji RCI probe, chief commissioner confirms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 8 — A former minister who was remanded over an investigation linked to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was released on Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) bail today. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the release, Sinar Harian reported today. “He (the former minister) has been released on MACC bail,” he said today.

items.title: Should political parties’ donors be protected? Azalina says issue among those being studied
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — If Malaysia were to have a law regulating donations to political parties, should it protect donors from being pursued by anti-corruption investigators after donating money? Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today that this was among the technical issues that have to be studied before steps are taken to introduce a political financing law in Malaysia. she said.

items.title: Nazir Razak, Musa Hitam say NEP fostered ‘tongkat culture’ among Malays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The New Economic Policy (NEP) fostered a culture of dependency among Malays and became too focused on ownership and government assistance, former CIMB Group chairman Tan Sri Nazir Razak and former deputy prime minister Tun Musa Hitam said today. Nazir said the NEP was intended to run for only 20 years and cited former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman’s description of it as a 20-year “handicap”. And when it goes on for too long, this ‘tongkat culture’ becomes deeply embedded,” said Nazir, the son of second prime minister Tun Abdul Razak Hussein.

items.title: Did the Negeri Sembilan MB sign decree to oust ruler? Claim sees state in renewed palace crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Negeri Sembilan has been thrust again into its unprecedented constitutional crisis, with claims that new Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim allegedly signed a proclamation to depose the state’s ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, just one day after swearing an oath of allegiance to him. According to the statement released by the four chieftains, Ismail met them on August 3 alongside throne contender Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar, the cousin of Tuanku Muhriz and son of the previous ruler. The chieftains alleged that Ismail signed the formal proclamation ousting Tuanku Muhriz during this gathering, paving the way for Tuanku Nadzaruddin’s installation.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt agencies to work together to tighten e-commerce rules, curb sale of prohibited goods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — The Communications Ministry is prepared to work with the Home Ministry, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, police and relevant agencies to strengthen e-commerce regulation and curb the sale of prohibited goods, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said most e-commerce platforms in Malaysia prohibit the sale of prohibited products, including drugs such as fentanyl, but expressed concern that one platform appeared to be too lax in allowing such products to be offered. “The accounts selling these prohibited products may be fake accounts,” he said.

items.title: Azalina: Malaysians want political funding law before GE16; political parties’ buy-in needed to avoid delay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — Malaysians have voiced their desire for Malaysia to have a political financing law to regulate political parties’ funding before the 16th general election, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said today. Azalina said the views of political parties would have to be obtained before the proposed political financing law is brought to Parliament, as it would be politicians in Parliament who would vote on whether to introduce such a law. Earlier in the speech, Azalina said BHEUU had taken over studies on the proposed political financing law since May 2023, and that the Cabinet had on September 8, 2023 agreed in principle to the enactment of the law and decided on further studies on the policy scope.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng hits PAS over failure to credit him for cutting lottery draws from 22 to eight a year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng has hit back at PAS over what he described as dishonest and hypocritical claims about DAP’s position on Islam, while pointing to his record of reducing special lottery draws when he was finance minister. In a Facebook post, Lim said PAS had failed to acknowledge that he was the first finance minister to reduce the number of special lottery draws from 22 to eight a year when Pakatan Harapan (PH) was in government from 2018 to 2020. “PAS is not honest and sincere when it fails to state that I was the first finance minister to reduce special lottery draws from 22 times to eight times a year during the PH government from 2018 to 2020,” he said.

items.title: IBS classrooms to ease overcrowding in Melaka schools, says deputy education minister
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 8 — The construction of additional classrooms using the Industrialised Building System (IBS) will enable special rooms currently used as temporary teaching and learning spaces to resume their original functions, said Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh. He said the move would help ease overcrowding while enabling schools to make better use of their existing facilities. “Some schools have had to convert special rooms, including music rooms and laboratories, into classrooms.

items.title: Blocked trails delayed six hikers’ return from Gunung Gerah, says Perak Fire Dept
items.summary: GERIK, 8 Sept — The closure and obstruction of hiking trails that have not been used for a long time were the main reasons why the six hikers took a longer time to make their way before they were found safe last night, after participating in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, on August 29. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the hikers found that the trails at Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat were closed due to these factors. “When they reached Gunung Beratoh and Gunung Sepat, the found that the trails to both these hills were closed as they had not been used by hikers for a long time.

items.title: AirAsia resumes most flights disrupted by Anak Krakatau eruption
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 8 — AirAsia has resumed flights to and from destinations affected by the Anak Krakatau volcanic eruption following the reopening of Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. “With Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport now reopened following its temporary closure since September 6, 2026, AirAsia has resumed affected services to and from Jakarta, with the exception of two flights on September 8, 2026,” it said in a statement today. The two affected flights are QZ178 from Jakarta (CGK) to Bandar Lampung (TKG) and QZ179 from Bandar Lampung to Jakarta.

items.title: Perak Fire Dept calls for age limits on children joining high-risk mountain expeditions
items.summary: GERIK, Sept 8 — The Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) recommends that the authorities review the standard operating procedure (SOP) regarding the age limit for children participating in extreme activities and hiking expeditions along challenging routes in mountainous areas. Previously, six climbers who participated in the Trans Gerah Expedition in Gunung Gerah, Kelantan who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing while climbing the mountain on August 29, were safely released from Pos Kemar, 10.20 this morning. The six victims involved, Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, as well as children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Post Health Clinic Kemar.

items.title: Police to record statements from six Gunung Gerah hikers after rescue
items.summary: BAGAN SERAI, Sept 8 — Police will record statements from six hikers in the Trans Gerah Expedition at Gunung Gerah, Kelantan, who were found safe yesterday after being reported missing during the hiking trip. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the six hikers would be taken to the Gerik District Police Headquarters (IPD) for documentation after being brought out from Pos Kemar. Asked whether the couple had committed an offence by bringing their two children on the hiking trip, Mohd Alwi said all four had valid permits.

items.title: Six Gunung Gerah hikers safely out of forest after days missing
items.summary: “All the victims and the SAR (search and rescue) team arrived safely at Pos Kemar at approximately 9.15pm last night. All the victims underwent a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic and rested at the facility. Previously, the six victims involved were found safe last night before being taken for a health check-up by medical officers at the Pos Kemar Health Clinic.

items.title: Malaysia plans 9GW of gas-fired power capacity by 2032 as demand rises, says economy minister
items.summary: Akmal Nasrullah said energy demand was showing an upward trend, driven by factors including population growth and higher consumption from energy-intensive sectors such as data centres. “In terms of the projection for energy demand, definitely we see a pattern of increase. Against this backdrop, Akmal Nasrullah said managing energy demand would become as crucial as managing energy supply over the next five to 10 years.

items.title: Selangor on track to top RM100b investment mark this year, says Amirudin
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 8 — Selangor is confident that the value of investments recorded by the state this year will exceed RM100 billion based on the current positive momentum, said Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said the state recorded about RM70 billion in investments up to mid-year, with the investment trend very encouraging. He said the development of new industrial areas, including NSIP in Sepang, as well as the development of a third port on Carey Island, is expected to continue to boost investment activities in Selangor.
